published.source: docs/PUBLIC_BENCHMARKS.md:380-394 (accuracy vs human label, no option shuffling)

notes: Records are exactly the ids in Nimble's committed subset manifest, converted by Nimble's own public_sources/helpsteer2.py; the selected records re-serialize to Nimble's dataset_sha256 (verified).

Option text is the criteria description only, in Nimble's key order; the key names are dropped (as in build_jeff.py / typed-decisions). Nimble's prompt (nimble/scoring/parallel_schema.py:95-101) and the Jev request ({key: description}, dataset_io.request_for) also showed the key name.
state and instructions are Nimble's input.state / decision.instructions unchanged; stage = Nimble domain.

score -> choice over the 5 ordered level descriptions (LEVELS), answer = level index + 1. Jev and Nimble were asked a native 5-level score with keys "0".."4". score: accuracy is exact-level match, as in Nimble's own table. nimble/evaluation/evaluate_pilot.py:51-62 assess(): gold = target_key(target) = str(level index), best = argmax over "0".."4", correct = best == gold; evaluate_public_jev.py:130-131 jev_row(): Jev prediction = student["prediction"] (the same argmax), correct = prediction == target. No tolerance. Nimble's doc (PUBLIC_BENCHMARKS.md:455-459) says to read the expected-level MAE for these subsets instead; gamebench/run.py gives per-option probabilities, so it can be computed from results.
source_sha256 matches the HF refs/convert/parquet export, not the repository's own json/jsonl.gz on main; both convert to the same dataset_sha256.
Nimble dropped 4 over-length row(s) (Qwen3.5-9B tokenizer, 2,048 tokens) before selection; the id list already reflects that. Nothing is truncated here.
